o: Return indices i (excluding first and last) where mountain[i] is strictly greater than both neighbors. With length ≤ 100, a direct scan is all that's needed. Example 2: indices 1 (4 > 1,3) and 3 (8 > 3,5).
k: Strict inequality on both sides; endpoints excluded.

a.i: Check each interior index against its two neighbors.
s: Collect i where mountain[i−1] < mountain[i] > mountain[i+1]

a.i: A peak occurs exactly where the difference sequence switches from + to −, i.e., d[i−1] > 0 and d[i] < 0 for d[i] = mountain[i+1] − mountain[i]. Equivalent, sometimes cleaner to reason about plateaus.
s: Peak at i where sign flips + to −

w: Any correct scan passes. Watch strictness: [2,4,4] has no peak because 4 is not strictly greater than the second 4.
